rejected.title: Sung narratives and songlines
card: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples have long held knowledge in songs, stories and places on Country. This knowledge has been passed on by speaking and singing across many generations.
A songline links a series of places along a route on Country. Each place is tied to a part of a song or story, so the places act as cues for the next part.
The knowledge held this way can include where to find water and food, how to care for Country, law, kinship and history. Different peoples hold their own songs and stories.
Psychologists see this as a memory system. It uses rhythm, melody, story and place together, much as mnemonics link new information to cues that are easier to recall.
rejected.remember: Songs, stories and places on Country work together as cues, so knowledge can be recalled and passed on.

a.q: Why does a songline help people to recall a large amount of knowledge?
opts: Each place on the route cues the next part of the song
The knowledge is reduced to one short rhyming phrase
The song is repeated until the words become automatic
Each person learns only one place and never the full song
a.why: A songline ties parts of a song or story to places in order, so each place cues what comes next. Repetition may be part of learning, but the card describes the links between song, story and place as what makes it work.
a.clue: Think about what the places do for the song.

b.q: A Year 12 student says a songline is only a song, so it cannot be a memory system. Which reply best shows the student's mistake?
opts: It links song, story and places, which act as recall cues
It is written down, so the song is not needed to recall it
It is a mnemonic made up recently for use in school
It holds facts about water only, so it is a narrow system
b.why: A songline joins music, story and places on Country, and these cues help people recall knowledge in order. It is not only a song, and it is not limited to water, as it can hold law, kinship, history and care of Country.
b.clue: Look at what a songline joins together, not only the song.

version.title: Sung narratives and songlines
card: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples have held and passed on knowledge across many generations through songs, stories, dance and places on Country.
A songline follows a route across Country. Each place along it is tied to part of a song or story, so reaching one place cues the next part.
Songlines can hold knowledge of water and food sources, seasons, law, kinship and history. Each people holds its own songs and stories, and some knowledge is shared only with certain people.
This works as a powerful memory system. Rhythm, melody, story and place act as linked cues, so a large body of knowledge can be recalled in order.
version.remember: Song, story and place work as linked cues, so knowledge can be held and passed on over generations.

a.q: Why can a songline hold so much knowledge in a set order?
opts: Each place along the route cues the next part
Knowledge is cut down to one short rhyming phrase
It is written down so no one needs to recall it
Each person learns one place and never the rest
a.why: A songline ties parts of a song or story to places in order, so arriving at each place cues what comes next. It is held by singing and telling, not in written records.
a.clue: Think about what the places do for the song.

b.q: A student says a songline is just a song, so it cannot be a memory system. Which reply best corrects the student?
opts: It joins melody, story and place as recall cues
It only holds facts about where to find water
It works because it was written for school use
It needs no cues, as the words are memorised
b.why: A songline links rhythm and melody with story and places on Country, and these linked cues help people recall large amounts of knowledge in order. It holds far more than water sources, including law, kinship and history.
b.clue: Look at what a songline joins together.

a.best: Each place along the route cues the next part

b.best: It joins melody, story and place as recall cues
